findings.claim: Objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the learning/score support is the observed score-node window [0.0,0.49] with 50 nodes and no extrapolation allowed.

Across all 20 landmark soft-mass features, no polynomial trend is accepted (polynomial_accepted=false for every row), relative node RMSE is large (0.50-0.99), and sign_changes range 4-10 with strong_sign_conflicts up to 17; whole-window z values are small (|z|<0.65). This indicates non-monotone, batch-conflicted coordinate contrast rather than a stable monotone drift.

landmark_10_soft_mass shows a reproducible within-window shape: values rise from about -0.38 z at t=0 to a peak near +1.0 z around t=0.19, then decline to about -0.37 z at t=0.49, with first_rate_z=+66.3 and last_rate_z=-11.6 and only 2 strong sign conflicts. This is a changing-contrast (rise-then-fall) profile, not a stationary target.

landmark_01_soft_mass shows a different within-window shape: it starts near +0.54 z at t=0, dips to about -0.89 z near t=0.05, then recovers to about +0.36 z at t=0.49, with first_rate_z=-26.0 and last_rate_z=+0.9 and 9 strong sign conflicts. The early rate sign is opposite to landmark_10_soft_mass.

hypotheses.direction: larger delta (more robust response) early in the window, smaller delta later, matching the rise-then-fall contrast
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_10_soft_mass curve over [0.0,0.49] is flat or monotone under an independent batch split, or if the mid-window peak does not reproduce, the time-dependent delta hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_10_soft_mass z-scored endpoint-world feature over observed score nodes [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score-node window; no extrapolation beyond [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_10_soft_mass coordinate contrast is time-dependent within the observed window: it rises to a mid-window maximum near t~0.19 and then falls, so a single constant curvature/delta applied uniformly over the window would not match the observed contrast shape.

hypotheses.direction: opposite early-window curvature response for landmark_01_soft_mass relative to landmark_10_soft_mass
hypotheses.falsifier: If landmark_01_soft_mass and landmark_10_soft_mass early-window rate signs agree under an independent batch split, the opposite-sign claim is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_01_soft_mass z-scored endpoint-world feature over observed score nodes [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score-node window; no extrapolation beyond [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_01_soft_mass coordinate contrast is also time-dependent but with an early dip and late recovery, so its early-window rate sign is opposite to landmark_10_soft_mass; a single uniform curvature schedule cannot match both landmarks' early-window behavior.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are not available; only continuous curves and trend/effect tables were read.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in role input; selection/survival evidence is not available as a measured final-benefit label.
The observed curves are z-scored endpoint-world coordinate proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is made.
Contrast curves and their time derivatives do not by themselves specify an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient; no absolute target is asserted here.
The registered recipes C1/C2/C3 are proposed interventions, not parameters learned from the observed slopes; no optimal parameter is claimed.
